To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dynamic responses of shallow spherical shells under axisymmetric impulsive loading are strongly influenced by the shell geometry, the loading conditions and the material properties.

(1) for a given shell, the dynamic response of the shell depends on the magnitude, location, and direction of the applied load; (2) the shell response is sensitive to the shell thickness, the shell radius, and the loading time; and (3) the shell response depends on the shell material properties, and the loading direction has the greatest influence on the shell response.
the dynamic deformation of a shallow spherical shell is strongly influenced by the shell's geometry and loading conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the dynamic response of spherical shells to impulsive loading.
the dynamic response of a thin spherical shell under asymmetric loadings.
the dynamic response of a shallow spherical shell to an axisymmetric impulsive loading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dynamic behavior of shallow spherical shells subjected to asymmetric impulsive loads is quite complex, and that the response is strongly dependent on the physical and loading conditions.
the impulsive loading at the apex of a shallow spherical shell produces a complex dynamic deformation response.
the dynamic deformation characteristics are very sensitive to the physical and loading parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for the case of impulsive concentrated tangential force, the dynamic response of shallow spherical shells are similar to that for shallow cylindrical shells.
the transient response of the shell is strongly affected by the shell thickness.

for shallow shells the impulsive moment loading produces a larger deflection and a higher peak value of the bending moment in the shell than the impulsive tangential force loading, and for a given shell the peak deflection and bending moment increase with increasing shell thickness, decreasing shell radius, and decreasing shell radius-to-thickness ratio.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamic deformation characteristics are significantly influenced by the loading and geometrical parameters.
the transient deformation characteristics of shallow shells are very much different than those of deep shells.
, for the case of a concentrated moment applied at the apex, the shell deforms as if the moment is applied at a distance of 2/3 of the shell thickness from the shell surface.
